context: The example starts with 13 elements. The maximum, 9, is at root index 0, and the last element, at index 12, is 5. In a max-heap, each parent's value must be at least as large as each child's.

The tree and array show the same storage. The array stores nodes in level order, from top to bottom and left to right within each level, starting at index 0. For a non-root position i, the parent index is (i−1)/2 rounded down. The child indices are 2i+1 and 2i+2. An out-of-bounds index means that child is absent. Indices distinguish nodes with equal values.
description: To pop, first swap the root at index 0 with the last element at index 12, then remove the former root from the end. This avoids shifting all subsequent elements as deleting the first entry would. Now sift down from the root. At each step, find the largest value among the current node and its children. If a child is larger, swap with the larger child. Only this choice guarantees that the new parent is at least as large as the other child. Stop when the current node is at least as large as its children or reaches a leaf.

Each storage table is titled by operation and step. A new table appears only when the array changes. Steps that only compare, stop, or clear highlighting refer by full title to the table with the same contents. Each step still gives the current size, root, and operation.

frames.announcement: Remove 9 from the end and save it as the return value. The heap array shrinks to 12 entries.
frames.explanation: There are now 12 entries, with 5 at the root. Remove 9 from the end, formerly index 12, and save it as the return value. Removing the rightmost leaf preserves the shape of the complete binary tree, but the 5 at root index 0 is smaller than its children and must sift down.

frames.title: Remove 9 from the end

frames.announcement: Compare 5, 8, and 7 at indices 0, 1, and 2. The larger child, 8 at index 1, exceeds 5, so a swap is pending.
frames.explanation: There are 12 entries, with 5 at the root. Compare 5 at index 0 with its left child, 8 at index 1, and its right child, 7 at index 2. The largest is 8 at index 1. It will be swapped in the next step. This step only compares values. For the unchanged array, see “Pop, step 3: array of 12 elements after removing the final 9.”
frames.key_state: There are 12 entries, with 5 at the root. Compare 5, 8, and 7 at indices 0, 1, and 2. The larger child, 8 at index 1, exceeds 5, so a swap is pending.
frames.title: Compare root 5 with its children

frames.announcement: Swap indices 0 and 1: 8 rises to the root, and 5 sinks to index 1.
frames.explanation: There are 12 entries, with 8 at the root. For the first downward swap, exchange 5 at index 0 with 8 at index 1. The new root, 8, exceeds its right child, 7 at index 2. The 5 moves to index 1, with left child 6 at index 3 and right child 7 at index 4.
frames.key_state: There are 12 entries, with 8 at the root. Swap indices 0 and 1: 8 rises to the root, and 5 sinks to index 1.

frames.title: Swap indices 0 and 1

frames.explanation: There are 12 entries, with 8 at the root. For the third downward swap, exchange 5 at index 4 with 6 at index 10. The 6 rises to index 4, and 5 reaches a leaf at index 10. Its child indices 21 and 22 are both out of bounds, so sifting stops.

frames.announcement: Pop complete: return 9. The root is 8, and 5 stops at index 10. There are 12 entries.
frames.explanation: There are 12 entries, with 8 at the root. Clear the highlighting and complete the pop by returning the 9 removed earlier. The 5 finishes at index 10, and all 12 entries again satisfy the max-heap property. For the unchanged array, see “Pop, step 9: array after the third downward swap.”
frames.key_state: There are 12 entries, with 8 at the root. All elements satisfy the max-heap property again. The 5 finishes at index 10. Return 9.

result: The pop returns 9. The value 5 sinks along indices 0→1→4→10 in three swaps.
summary: After removing the maximum, restore the max-heap by sifting down from the root, swapping with the larger child.
title: Popping the root of a max-heap
